Mom's Current Care Information, in One Place

A one-page inventory of the papers, lists and phone numbers you already have, and the ones you don't.

Download PDF

The medication list is in a drawer, the discharge summary is in a text message, and the therapist's name is in your sister's phone.

This page doesn't ask you to understand any of it. It asks where each thing is, how recent it is, and who has it.

What to collectWhere it isIts dateWho has it
Discharge instructions, in writing
Summary of her current health
Medication list: prescriptions, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins and supplements
What changed in her medications during the stay
Names and phone numbers to call with questions
Follow-up appointments
Therapies or services involved, and their schedule
Equipment that was recommended, and who is arranging it
Her doctors and her pharmacy
Other records or test results you were given

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

What's missing, and who will ask for it

Anything above with an empty line. Put a name next to each.

For example No written summary of her current health. David will call the hospital on Monday.

How to use it

  • Write the date printed on each item. If it has no date, write “undated” and ask for a current copy.
  • Don't rewrite or summarize a document here. Just say where it is.
  • Bring this page and the documents to the next appointment.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what any record or instruction means. If you read something you don't understand, that's a question for the person who wrote it.

Ready for the next step?

You know where everything is and what's missing. The care interview uses what you've collected: it walks you through Mom's situation area by area and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Where this comes from
